We will also display the analysis using a scatterplot. # Results ::: {#5d71c0e4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} corr_val = np.array(df[['alcohol', 'ins_premium']].corr())[0][1] print(corr_val) narrative = "a very strong negative correlation" if corr_val > .8: narrative = "a very strong positive correlation" elif corr_val > .4: narrative = "a moderate positive correlation" elif corr_val > 0: narrative = "a weak positive correlation" elif corr_val > -.4: narrative = "a weak negative correlation" elif corr_val > .8: narrative = "a moderate negative correlation" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` -0.1706119736858754 ``` ::: ::: Using the simple Pearson correlation approach, these data produce a correlation coefficient of \-0\.1706; given this result, we conclude that there is a weak negative correlation between rate of alcohol-impaired drivers and cost of car insurance premiums. ::: {#cell-fig-alc-prem-scatterplot .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (6, 3.5)) sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'ins_premium', x = 'alcohol') plt.xlabel('Percentage of Alcohol-Impaired Drivers') plt.ylabel('Car Insurance Premiums ($)') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![A scatterplot of alcohol-impaired drivers and insurance premiums](index_files/figure-html/fig-alc-prem-scatterplot-output-1.png){#fig-alc-prem-scatterplot width=528 height=320} ::: ::: As show in in @fig-alc-prem-scatterplot we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between the rate of alcohol-impaired drivers and cost of car insurance premiums. # Discussion We have established that there is a weakly negative correlation between rate of alcohol-impaired drivers and insurance premiums.
